description: History of the Olympics, sports categories, and notable achievements

ancient_olympics.end: 393 CE; banned by Emperor Theodosius I (Christian Roman Emperor)

modern_olympics.revival: Pierre de Coubertin; 1896 Athens; 14 nations, 241 athletes

olympic_principles.olympism: Philosophy combining sport with culture and education
olympic_principles.olympic_motto: Citius, Altius, Fortius – Communiter (Faster, Higher, Stronger – Together)
olympic_principles.five_rings: Represent five continents; blue, yellow, black, green, red on white
olympic_principles.olympic_flame: Lit in Olympia, Greece; carried by relay to host city
olympic_principles.amateurism_vs_professionalism: Professionals now allowed in all sports; changed 1988–1992

recent_olympics.2020_tokyo: Held 2021; COVID delayed; first with spectator restrictions
recent_olympics.2022_beijing: Winter Olympics; boycotted by some nations diplomatically
recent_olympics.2024_paris: Summer Olympics; Seine River swim events; breaking debut and farewell
